questionsToConsider: Who is running the survey, and will you say so in the greeting? People answer more openly when they know.
Is the focus local, national or one specific issue, and do the ranking items match it?
Do the options on every question cover the full range of views, including a neutral or unsure choice?
Which demographic questions do you really need to compare groups, and can they stay optional?
guide.howToUseResponses: Start with the ranking, since the order of issues is the clearest single result. Then split the priorities grid and the trust score by age group and political leaning to see where groups agree and where they don't. Read the reasons given by people who feel things are on the wrong track, and group them into themes before reporting. When you publish results, report the question wording alongside the numbers so readers can judge them fairly.
customizeSteps: Name who is running the survey and why in the greeting, and replace the ranking items with the issues that are live in your area.
Adjust the priorities grid to the decisions your local council, school board or parliament is actually facing.
Share the link in places that reach a mix of views, not only your own supporters, and export the answers to CSV to analyse them.

faqs.q: How do you write unbiased political survey questions?
faqs.a: Describe each issue in plain, neutral terms, give balanced answer options and always include a way to say you're unsure. Avoid words that signal which answer you prefer.

faqs.q: What should a political survey ask?
faqs.a: Which issues matter most, how people feel about the direction of things, how much they trust their representatives and a few optional background questions to compare groups.

faqs.q: Should a political survey ask about party or voting?
faqs.a: Only if you need it to compare groups. This template asks about general political leaning with a prefer-not-to-say option, rather than naming parties, and keeps it optional.

faqs.q: Can I keep political survey responses anonymous?
faqs.a: Yes. This template never asks for a name or email. If you add contact details, make them optional and say why you are asking.

doc.title: Political opinion survey
doc.description: Ask people where they stand on public issues, in neutral wording that leaves room for every view.

blocks.title: Hi! We're asking people in the area about the public issues that matter to them. It takes about four minutes, and every view is welcome.
Which town, city or area do you live in?
In general, do you think things in your area are heading in the right direction or on the wrong track?
What makes you feel things are on the wrong track?
Put these issues in order of how much they matter to you, most important first.
How much of a priority should each of these be for local government?
How much do you trust your elected officials to act in residents' best interests?
How often do you vote in elections?
Where do you usually get news about politics?
Which of these best describes your political views?
blocks.description: Optional, and only used to compare answers across groups.
